reference.title: TLV757P 1A, Low IQ, Small-Size, Low-Dropout Regulator (SBVS322C, revised March 2024)

pins.name: IN
pins.note: Input pin (datasheet type I). A capacitor of 1 µF or larger is required from IN to GND; effective capacitance at the pin must exceed 0.47 µF. Absolute maximum VIN 6.0 V; operating range 1.45 V to 5.5 V (Table 5-3).

pins.name: GND
pins.note: Ground pin (datasheet type —). The DBV package has no exposed thermal pad; heat is conducted through the leads and body (RθJA 100.8 °C/W on EVM, 231.1 °C/W on JEDEC, Table 5-3).

pins.name: EN
pins.note: Enable pin, active high (datasheet type I): enable above VHI = 1 V, shut down below VLO = 0.3 V (Section 5.5). If shutdown is not required connect EN to IN. The EN pin is independent of IN; if EN is driven above VIN limit the EN toggle frequency to below 10 kHz (Section 6.3.2). No internal pull-up or pull-down on EN is stated.

pins.name: NC
pins.note: No internal connection (DBV pin 4). Leave floating or use as a mechanical / keep-out pad only; do not assign an electrical net.

pins.name: OUT
pins.note: Regulated output (datasheet type O), fixed 3.3 V for this ordering option (TLV757 33 = 3.3 V, Table 8-1). A capacitor of 1 µF or larger is required from OUT to GND (max 200 µF). The P suffix means active output discharge: when disabled the output is pulled to ground through an internal ~120 Ω switch (Section 6.3.2). Absolute maximum VOUT is VIN + 0.3 V or 6.0 V, whichever is smaller; observe the reverse-current limits of Section 7.1.4.

Now add rules. Rules for this LDO:
1. EN must be connected/enabled — warn when EN not used as enable? Actually rules read assignment of functions. Let's craft rules:

- `en_must_be_driven`: warn if EN's active function is not "EN" — but EN only has one function, so it would never be inactive... Rule evaluation with each function active. Rule referencing function("EN") — with default it's "EN". Let's write a rule: if !active("EN","EN") { warn("EN ...") } else { ok() }. Hmm, that gives ok in the "with each function active" evaluation and warn in no-selection? Default function for EN is EN, so without selections it's active → ok. Fine.

Better rules relevant to this part:
1. `en_enable_warn`: warn when EN not enabled → since EN has only one function it can't be different. Instead, warn that EN defaults nothing: "EN has no internal pull; it must be driven above 1 V..." — a warn always? Rules must end with verdicts. Could write: `if !active("EN", "EN") { warn(...) } else { warn(...) }`? That's silly. Let me design meaningful rules:

Rule A: `nc_must_stay_float` — forbid connecting NC: `if active("NC", "NC") { warn("NC (pin 4) has no internal connection...") } else { forbid("...") }`. Hmm — with default, NC's only function is active, so at preview without selections it would be a warn (fine, warn isn't blocking). If someone removed it... can't. Let's just do warn always: `if active("NC","NC") { warn("DBV pin 4 is NC — no internal connection; leave floating or use as a spare mechanical pad only.") } else { forbid("DBV pin 4 must not carry an electrical function; it has no internal connection.") }`. Wait, forbid when NC is not active means it's blocking. Preview evaluates "with each function it names literally made active" and "without selections" — without selections NC's only function is active → warn. So no blocking finding. Hmm, but the requirement says a rule that fails in any of these is a blocking finding — a warn is not a failure presumably. Let me be careful: keep it simple.

Rule B: `input_capacitor_required` — require(...) is "reported as unmet until it holds" — that's a rule requiring something true-ish. Better to use warn: "IN requires ≥1 µF capacitor to GND". Rule: `if !role("power","input") { warn("...") } else { warn("...") }`? Simplest: always warn with a design note? Rules that always warn are acceptable (verdict warn, not blocking).

Maybe better to write rules expressing real constraints:

1. `in_out_caps`: warn always (a note): "IN and OUT each require ≥1 µF ceramic capacitor (effective >0.47 µF) — Table 4-1 note 1."
Script: `if role("power","input") && role("power","output") { warn("...") } else { warn("...") }` — hmm, both branches same. Let me instead: `if used("power") { warn(...) } else { ok() }`. Since power is used by default (IN/GND/OUT active), preview shows warn. Fine and legit.

2. `en_drive`: "EN has no internal pull-up: it floats to shutdown; drive EN > VHI (1 V) to enable, or tie EN to IN if shutdown not needed. If EN > VIN, limit EN toggle frequency to 10 kHz." Script: `if active("EN","EN") && !role("power","input") { warn(...) } else if ...` — need branches to all end in verdicts; simplest:
`if used("enable") { warn("EN has no internal pull-up (no pull stated in the datasheet): leave it below VLO = 0.3 V for shutdown, or drive above VHI = 1 V to enable; if shutdown is not required, connect EN to IN.") } else { ok() }`.

3. `reverse_current`: warn when output used and input used: "VOUT must not exceed VIN + 0.3 V; reverse current into OUT can damage the device (Section 7.1.4)."
`if role("power","output") && role("power","input") { warn(...) } else { ok() }`

4. `no_shutdown_without_discharge`? Maybe a rule about the EN pin independent of IN and abs max 6 V: `if used("enable") { warn(...) } else { ok() }`.

5. Ground rule: DBV has no thermal pad — GND is the only ground path; warn that thermal performance depends on copper on the GND lead. `if role("power","ground") { warn("DBV has no exposed thermal pad: heat leaves only through the leads; the layout example (Figure 7-7) connects pin 2 to a ground plane.") } else { ok() }`.

6. Fixed output: forbid using OUT as an adjustable feedback? There's no FB pin. Could add rule: `forbid` if ... hmm not necessary.

Also required: rules types listed (strapping, flash, debug, USB, functions that can't be used together) — those are MCU-specific; for an LDO, adapt: I'll provide the relevant ones (enable/absmax/NC/capacitor/ground/thermal). And add one "forbid" rule that's meaningful: OUT must not be shorted to IN? Can't express. Perhaps: forbid connecting GND and IN to the same net? Not expressible via API (no net identity check). Hmm.

I could add a forbid rule for NC pin being used as power: `if active("NC","NC") && used("power") { warn(...) } else { ok() }` — a warn for using NC while power is used. Actually more meaningful: `if active("NC","NC") { warn("NC has no internal connection...") } else { forbid("...") }` — but the else forbid could trigger at preview? Rules are evaluated: without selections (NC active → warn), with each function active (NC active → warn), so never the forbid branch. Actually if NC is never active it'd be a blocking finding, but that can't happen since NC is its only function. I'll use this pattern to express "NC must not be reassigned."

Let me be safe and avoid the else-forbid pattern; use requires? Simpler: warn-only + one forbid for a genuine conflict: `excludes("NC.NC", "power.input")`? excludes takes "A.f" pairs — NC.NC and power.input both active would forbid. That would be a blocking finding at preview because default has both active (NC's only function active and power input active). So not good.

OK, keep the warn set plus one forbid rule that only fires when something impossible happens... Preview evaluation makes forbids risky. I'll include one forbid-style rule keyed on the enable role not taken? e.g. "the regulator must be enabled to regulate" — that's a require: `requires("OUT.OUT", "enable.enable")`? requires("A.f","B.g"): require with generated message when A.f active and B.g not, else ok. report.summary: Imported a 5-terminal pinout for the DBV SOT-23-5 variant only (IN, GND, EN, NC, OUT per Table 4-1) with two peripherals (power: input/output/ground; enable: enable) and 7 design-rule warnings (input/output capacitor requirement, EN thresholds and no internal pull, EN-above-VIN frequency limit, reverse-current limit at OUT, no thermal pad on DBV, NC pin unused, enable needed for regulation). Built the package and footprint from the DBV0005A mechanical drawing and its example board layout using the built-in tabbed starter row "SOT-23-5": body 2.9 x 1.6 mm, lead span 2.8 mm, pitch 0.95 mm, 5 lands 0.6 x 1.1 mm at 2.6 mm row-centre span, generated 3D model (no built-in part file covers a SOT-23-5), text-only can marking "1FKF" from the package addendum. Everything checks without blocking findings; the 5 imported terminals are still unreviewed, which is expected. Row positions and body height were derived arithmetically from the drawing's min/max ranges — see the confidence flags and open questions below.

values.item: Pin assignment DBV: 1 IN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 NC, 5 OUT
values.value: 5 pins, as listed
5 (no exposed thermal pad on DBV; only DYD and DRV have one)
IN = I, OUT = O, EN = I, GND and NC = "—"
VHI = 1 V, VLO = 0.3 V; IEN = 10 nA at 5.5 V; no internal pull-up/pull-down on EN stated
10 kHz (applies when EN is driven above VIN)
1 µF min each (0.47 µF min effective at the pin after 50 % derating), COUT max 200 µF
~120 Ω internal pulldown from OUT to GND when disabled / in UVLO
absolute maximum VOUT = VIN + 0.3 V or 6.0 V (smaller); Schottky protection shown
